You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Thistledown grocer","question":"Can the stock manager order jars against a shipment record?","claims":{"A":"The G11 pallet was wet on arrival.","B":"G11 arrived with six cartons.","C":"Shipment G11 contained at least 96 saleable jars at arrival."},"sources":{"S1":"the packing plan specifies 16 jars per carton. Staff did not count or inspect the jars and described 96 as the expected saleable count.","S2":"courier unloading receipt confirms six G11 cartons arrived.","S3":"pallet inspection confirms the pallet was dry on arrival."},"follow_up":{"S4":"an independent sealed-camera count and inspection at arrival confirms 96 saleable jars in G11."}}

message.content: {"claims":{"A":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S3"],"confidence":90},"B":{"status":"supported","citations":["S2"],"confidence":95},"C":{"status":"supported","citations":["S1","S4"],"confidence":98}},"note":"Claim A is contradicted by the pallet inspection (S3) showing the pallet was dry, not wet. Claim B is supported by the courier unloading receipt (S2) confirming six cartons arrived. Claim C is supported by the packing plan and staff expectation (S1) and decisively confirmed by the independent sealed-camera count (S4) showing 96 saleable jars. Thus, the stock manager can rely on shipment records for ordering jars."}

parsed.note: Claim A is contradicted by the pallet inspection (S3) showing the pallet was dry, not wet. Claim B is supported by the courier unloading receipt (S2) confirming six cartons arrived. Claim C is supported by the packing plan and staff expectation (S1) and decisively confirmed by the independent sealed-camera count (S4) showing 96 saleable jars. Thus, the stock manager can rely on shipment records for ordering jars.
